subject: Retention boundary questions — prompts vs. generated outputs (Q&A)
messages:
From: Sanjay Mehta <sanjay@datacorp.com>
To: olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com, neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2027-06-30T08:12:00+01:00
Subject: Clarification on default retention for prompts vs outputs

Hi Olga,

Quick question as we finalize our security review: by default when using Redwood's hosted API, what exactly is retained and for how long? Specifically:
- Are raw request/response pairs (the literal prompt we send and the model's output) stored by default?
- Do you treat the customer's "prompts" differently from "generated outputs" for retention or processing?
- Where (region) are those artifacts stored for EU customers?

We're trying to map this to our data lifecycle: which items we need to classify as PII, retention windows, and what the delete/removal process looks like. The contracting team asked me to attach the SOC2 summary you previously sent — attaching here for easy reference.

Thanks,
Sanjay
Sanjay Mehta
Lead Security Engineer, DataCorp Analytics

From: olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com
To: Sanjay Mehta <sanjay@datacorp.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com, neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2027-06-30T09:05:00+01:00
Subject: Re: Clarification on default retention for prompts vs outputs

Hi Sanjay — thanks for the clear questions, happy to clarify at a high level and loop in the privacy/compliance owners for anything you want in writing. Short answers up front, details below:

- Default hosted (self-serve) behavior: raw request/response bodies (what you send as prompt and what the model returns) are retained by default for 30 days unless you opt out.
- Prompts vs outputs: we classify the inbound text you send as "prompts/inputs" and the model-generated text as "outputs/derived responses." Both are kept under the 30-day default retention for raw bodies, but we maintain aggregated telemetry (tokens, latency, error rates) for 180 days for operational analytics.
- EU residency: for customers who select an EU region, the raw content and short-term logs are stored in EU-hosted backing stores; longer-term telemetry aggregates are also stored in EU where applicable.

Options for stricter controls (available per contract / for Dedicated & Private customers):
- Opt-out of content retention for hosted: you can enable "no retention" for request/response bodies; we then avoid storing raw prompts/outputs beyond ephemeral processing for inference.
- Dedicated & Private: by default there is no content retention outside customer-controlled storage; retention policies are managed by the customer infra.

Deletion & audit:
- For hosted customers, we provide a deletion API (DELETE /v1/records) that triggers a purge of raw request/response artifacts within 48 hours and an audit log entry.
- For contractual/eDiscovery requests we provide an export and attest path (may require DPA/scoped access).

I'll drop a short matrix from our privacy team to clarify edge cases (embeddings, cached KV, safety logs) — tagging Marissa/Neha to add detail.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com

Thanks Olga — that helps. A couple quick follow-ups so we can finalize our control matrix:
1) Embeddings: if we call embeddings APIs, are the vectors or the source text retained by default?
2) KV cache / prefix cache: anything cached at the inference runtime (KV cache) — does that persist to storage that would fall under the retention windows you mentioned?
3) Are prompts/outputs used for model improvements or safety tuning by default, or is that only if we enable quality monitoring?

If you can confirm those three, and point me to the endpoint for the deletion API and the expected SLA for attestations, we'll be able to close our review.

Appreciate it,
Sanjay

From: marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
To: olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com, neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2027-06-30T13:45:00+01:00
Subject: Internal: retention matrix (answers for DataCorp)

Olga / Neha — drafting a short, customer-facing reply below and attaching the matrix. Key points to include in the reply to Sanjay:

- Embeddings: by default, embeddings service stores the source text transiently during compute; vectors are retained if you call the embeddings store or enable semantic search indexing. Default hosted behavior retains embedding vectors for 30 days; customers can opt out or control retention via API.

- KV / prefix cache: runtime KV cache is ephemeral and lives in memory on the inference host; we do not persist KV cache to long-term object storage by default. If you enable session persistence (a dedicated feature), then session artifacts are stored and subject to the configured retention window.

- Model improvement / safety: prompts + outputs are available to our product safety/quality pipelines by default for up to 90 days for sampling and regression detection unless the customer enables the "no retention" flag. We mark data used in ML improvement pipelines as aggregated/anonymized where possible and exclude PII based on automated detectors and manual review controls. This is a distinction from raw request/response retention (30 days) vs. quality/safety retention (90 days).

- Deletion API: DELETE /v1/ingestion/records?customer_id=<id> — typical purge completion 24-72 hours; we return a job id for attestations. For legal exports/attestations we'll generate an audit report within 7 business days (may vary by contract).

I'll attach the retention-matrix.xlsx for their records (covers raw bodies, telemetry, embeddings, caches, and audit timelines). Suggest we send a single reply that enumerates the three answers and links to the matrix and the HubSpot record.
